summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted for high-dose Cytoxan as part of stem cell mobilization for multiple myeloma. He had developed new bilateral leg edema and a 28-pound weight gain, which was attributed to urinary retention due to inadequate self-catheterization of his neo-bladder, draining 2 liters upon Foley placement. Chemotherapy proceeded as planned after confirmation of no active infection. He spiked a low-grade fever and had transient diarrhea, but cultures were negative and symptoms resolved. He was monitored for cardiac and pulmonary risks, both of which were stable. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue daily catheterization, take ciprofloxacin prophylaxis, and follow up with his oncology and urology teams.
